primary_question: Which of the seven healing schedules work, which heal best (quality at equal budget) and which heal most efficiently (tokens/FLOPs/wall time). Producing a model, reaching stock 0.8B quality, and the damage operator are secondary: they serve the schedule comparison.
primary_metrics: headline (user, 2026-11-11): training FLOPs (plus decision FLOPs for adaptive arms) to the confirmed 25% gap rung. Also reported: fraction of the gap closed at equal training FLOPs; FLOPs, tokens and wall time to the 25/50/75/100% rungs; final test CE and downstream scores. Tokens are secondary because arms spend very different FLOPs per token.
status: light-student comparison complete (2026-11-13, one seed); write-up in findings.md. Heavy v3 pilot done (runs/pilot-v2, reports/pilot-v2).

primary.selection: activation (Minitron-style) on teacher calibration statistics; optional RMSNorm gain rescale kept only if it lowers probe controller CE

flop_convention: PyTorch registered matmul/attention/convolution forward+backward; excludes elementwise, normalization, optimizer; not exact total arithmetic
target_rule: native Qwen3.5-0.8B validation CE (held-out biomed+argument), frozen before the first healing arm; two consecutive validation evaluations at or below it. Secondary threshold native + 0.10 nats derived from the same curves.

controller.adaptive_error: block with largest added discrepancy sum(max(0, e_i - e_{i-1}))
controller.adaptive_plateau: blocks in order, wrapping; move when relative endpoint improvement < 0.01 between decisions or after 2x equal budget share
controller.adaptive_error_cap: v3 (2026-11-09): a block that has received max_block_share (2) x its equal share of the budget in total is not eligible; the heavy pilot (no cap) spent ~90% on layers 0-3

optimizer.name: AdamW
optimizer.state_policy: persist per parameter across window changes
optimizer.warmup: linear over each parameter group's first 32 updates (embedding, final norm, each layer)

precision: FP32 trainable weights (decoder layers, tied embedding/head, final norm) and optimizer states; BF16 autocast; teacher BF16
trainable_parameters: all decoder layers; tied embedding/output head when a window touches either end of the stack; final norm when a window ends at the last layer

downstream.gsm8k: test, fixed hashed order, first 128, greedy, thinking off, 1024 new tokens (v2 baselines used 384)

data.format: chat domains through the teacher chat template; instruction/math/math_word/reasoning with non-empty <think> blocks closing into the answer and <|im_end|>
data.shares: equal per in-mix domain; a short domain's shortfall spread over the others
data.splits: item-level salted hash; in-mix 3% controller, 3% test_in_domain, 1% calibration, rest train; held-out domains half validation, half test
data.contamination: items sharing a 13-word n-gram with (or containing a whole 8-12-word) GSM8K test, ARC validation/test or MMLU test question are dropped
data.replaces: WikiText-2 (version 1): too far from what an instruction/thinking chat model is for, and train/validation shared a domain with the stopping rule

canary: every GPU job checks the untouched teacher per-sequence CE on 4 calibration sequences against a CPU FP32 reference (0.05 nats) and the first passing GPU result (0.01 nats), at start and end; failures exit 3 and are rerun in a fresh process

pilot_v2.result: no arm reached the target; best final test CE 6.33 (overlap) from damaged 8.94

followup_branching.status: planned follow-up; runs only after the main seven-arm comparison
followup_branching.question: Does the best schedule depend on the healing phase (early, mid, late)?
followup_branching.why_branching: Independent arms spread their plan over the whole budget, so what an arm does in a phase depends on its budget, and its speed in a phase mixes schedule quality with the state the schedule left behind. Branching from one shared checkpoint removes both confounds.
design: One trunk run saves checkpoints at the first evaluation closing 25%, 50% and 75% of the validation gap (--checkpoint-gaps).
From each checkpoint, all seven schedules continue with equal budgets and fresh schedules (--init-from); a checkpoint carries weights, Adam state, per-group update counts and the data position.
Score each branch on the same ladder as the main arms (thresholds from the trunk's damaged start): FLOPs and tokens to the next rung, and gap closed at the end of its budget.
Then race a composite (best early -> best mid -> best late) against the best single schedule run end to end, over several seeds.
open_choices: trunk schedule (proposed: the main study's best single schedule)
followup_branching.tested: test_branch_resume_matches_uninterrupted_run: trunk checkpoint + branch equals an uninterrupted run bit for bit on CPU

followup_light_damage.status: now the main line of work (user, 2026-11-09): one-seed pilot running via drivers/pilot-light.sh
followup_light_damage.question: Do the schedules rank the same in the fine-tuning end of the gap (the last ~25%), which the heavily damaged 0.8B student cannot reach on a practical budget?
design: Prune the same teacher by at most 25% of non-embedding parameters (user rule, 2026-11-09), with the same activation-based selection and norm rescale. CPU-probed candidates: hidden 1792/FFN 4800 (25.1%), hidden 1792/FFN 5376 (19.7%), hidden 1920/FFN 5248 (15.3%).
Choose the cut from CPU start-CE probes. One option is to match the heavy student's late-stage loss, so a fresh light cut can be compared with a heavily damaged model healed to the same loss.
No stock model exists at these sizes, so the 100% rung is the 2B teacher's validation CE (2.55). The gap ladder and efficiency metrics are otherwise unchanged.
Same seven schedules, same FLOP accounting, seeds as in the main study.
followup_light_damage.relation_to_branching: Complementary. Branching from a 75% checkpoint studies the late phase of the same heavily damaged model (the residual error left after healing). A light cut studies fresh, diffuse pruning damage of small size.
followup_light_damage.note: Parameter counts include the 248k-token tied embedding.

chosen_cut.note: user chose ~25% and skipped the size sweep to keep exploration quick

pilot.optimizer_check: joint at batch 1/lr 1e-4, batch 1/lr 3e-5, batch 4/lr 1e-4; lowest final controller CE sets batch and lr for all seven arms; that check run is reused as the joint arm
pilot.why_32_sequences: on the heavy pilot, 16- vs 32-sequence validation CE for the fixed arm differed by 0.2, as large as gaps between arms

followup_local_global.status: running (user, 2026-11-10): drivers/followup-local-global.sh; the remaining 1M-token pilot evaluations are paused
followup_local_global.question: Light-pilot joint gained fastest early then drifted; fixed was slow but steady. Do combinations of global (whole-network) and local (fixed-block) training beat fixed, and does feeding each block the teacher's stream (no student prefix) heal more per FLOP?
followup_local_global.settings: as the light pilot: seed 17, 6e15 training FLOPs, lr 3e-5, batch 1, 8 evaluations of 32 sequences; compared with runs/pilot-light/fixed-seed17 and joint-seed17

arms.global_fixed: schedules.global_fixed: whole network for the first of 7 equal FLOP shares, then the six 4-layer blocks bottom to top
arms.alternating: schedules.alternating: fixed sweep; the last 20% of each of 24 equal FLOP slices trains the whole network (about 80/20 local/global by FLOPs)
arms.fixed-teacher: fixed, --window-inputs teacher: each block reads the teacher's residual stream after its previous layer, restricted to the student's residual coordinates, and the student prefix is not run (its FLOPs are not spent)
arms.fixed-ramp: fixed, --window-inputs ramp: teacher-fed with probability 1 - (position inside the block's FLOP share), so each block starts teacher-fed and ends on its own prefix (BERT-of-Theseus-style progressive replacement applied to window inputs)

followup_local_global.teacher_inputs_note: Each training row is used once at this budget, so caching teacher activations would not save teacher FLOPs here; computing them per step is equivalent. The saving measured is the skipped student prefix.
followup_local_global.evaluation: Always the student's own full stream (cumulative replacement), plus the baseline-format evaluation (evaluate.py, GSM8K at 1024 tokens) of each final model.

followup_random.question: Do random windows (every step, or kept until their own loss gains or stalls), a decaying learning rate for joint, or a coarse-to-fine hierarchy beat fixed and joint on training FLOPs to the 25% rung?
followup_random.settings: seed 17, 6e15 training FLOPs, lr 3e-5, batch 1, 24 evaluation points (every 0.25e15; includes the pilot's 8)

arms.joint-cosine: joint, lr cosine-decayed to 0 over the budget
arms.random: new random window every step: width uniform 1..24, start uniform
arms.random_dwell: random window kept until EMA(0.9) of its training loss is 5% under the mean of its first 5 losses (gain), no 1% new best for 15 steps (stall), or 60 steps (cap); flips logged in controller-decisions.json
arms.coarse_to_fine: hierarchical reversed: 6 equal stages of widths 24, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, each swept bottom to top

followup_random.notes: coarse_to_fine's first sixth is plain joint, which crosses 25% before it switches, so it ties joint on FLOPs to 25%; it is run for later rungs and final quality (briefly dropped and restored by the user, 2026-11-11). Per-step training loss varies 10-30% at batch 1, so random_dwell triggers are noisy by construction.
followup_random.findings: joint-cosine is the best light-student arm: first to 40% (0.76e15), lowest final loss (3.142, 46.7% of the gap), best ARC-E and GSM8K; plain joint's drift was its constant learning rate. Global-first arms reach 25% by ~0.5e15, block-local arms need >=2.25e15. Narrowing to local windows after global training hurts (coarse_to_fine jumped from 3.187 to 3.331 at the width-16 switch and never recovered). Random windows reach 25% fast but plateau and never reach 40%. One seed; the 25% rung is resolution-limited. Full table in README 'Light-student results'.

pilot_v3_heavy.settings: seed 17, 6e15 training FLOPs, lr 1e-4, batch 1, 6 evaluations of 16 sequences
pilot_v3_heavy.result: best final validation CE adaptive_plateau 4.445 and fixed 4.454 (61% of the gap to stock 0.8B) from 7.055; joint fastest at the first evaluation (5.38) then flat at 4.8-4.95
